nodes.description: Account shared between members (example 'Gedeeld met Partner', BE12 7730). When a member also links the account at the bank, all members see the same transactions and the same planning; a member sees the account history but not the other member's personal accounts. Roles on the account include manager (beheerder) and Lid with edit permission. One consent's connection can take over for the shared account when the partner links it too.
nodes.rationale: Shared accounts expose only the shared account's data, never the members' personal accounts.

nodes.label: Trusted device (90-day sign-in)
nodes.description: After password and e-mail code a device becomes trusted for the Saldo account and stays signed in until the user signs it out or it is unused for 90 days. Method shown as 'Wachtwoord en e-mailcode' or 'Home Assistant en e-mailcode'. Managed in Instellingen, Toestellen. A notice is always sent for each new device, except the device that created the account via setup link or invitation.
nodes.rationale: Saldo does not look up place or IP, so the mail never names a location; the 'not you' note carries the action: sign the device out and choose a new password.

nodes.label: Invitation link (7 days, single use)
nodes.description: An admin invites a person by e-mail; the one-time link to /uitnodiging/<token> is valid for 7 days and lets the invitee create an account. The invitee sees only own accounts and accounts they share. An unexpected invitation can be ignored.
nodes.rationale: Account creation is invitation-only on a household instance.

nodes.label: Password reset link (admin-created, 1 hour, single use)
nodes.description: An administrator creates a one-time link to /wachtwoord/<token>, valid for one hour after creation. After choosing the new password the user logs in as usual with an e-mail code. If the user did not ask for it, they contact the administrator.
nodes.norm_label: password reset link (admin-created, 1 hour, single use)
nodes.rationale: Passwords are reset by an administrator on request rather than via self-service e-mail reset.
